content:
Extract structured profile data from this resume text. Be thorough and extract ALL information - and copy, never infer: every name, title, employer, date, figure, skill and sentence comes out as the resume writes it. A profile with a gap where the resume says nothing is correct; a profile with something the resume does not say is not.

RESUME TEXT:
[[resumeText]]

Extract and return a JSON object with these EXACT fields:
{
  "name": "Full Name",
  "title": "The headline the resume states under the name (else the most recent job title, as written)",
  "contact": {
    "email": "email@example.com",
    "phone": "+1234567890",
    "location": "City, Country",
    "linkedin": "https://linkedin.com/in/username (or null if not found)"
  },
  "summary": "The resume's own summary paragraph, as written (or empty string when it has none)",
  "experience": [
    {
      "title": "Job Title",
      "company": "Company Name",
      "startDate": "MM/YYYY",
      "endDate": "MM/YYYY or Present",
      "location": "City, Country",
      "description": "Brief role description, in the resume's own words",
      "achievements": ["Achievement 1", "Achievement 2", "..."]
    }
  ],
  "skills": ["Skill1", "Skill2", "..."],
  "softSkills": ["Soft skill 1", "Soft skill 2", "..."],
  "strengths": [
    {
      "title": "Strength Name",
      "description": "Brief description of the strength"
    }
  ],
  "education": [
    {
      "degree": "Degree Name (e.g., Bachelor's in Computer Science)",
      "institution": "University Name",
      "startDate": "MM/YYYY",
      "endDate": "MM/YYYY",
      "location": "City, Country"
    }
  ],
  "certifications": [
    {
      "name": "Certification Name",
      "issuer": "Issuing Organization",
      "date": "MM/YYYY"
    }
  ],
  "projects": [
    {
      "name": "Project Name",
      "role": "Your role or the technologies, as the resume states it",
      "startDate": "MM/YYYY",
      "endDate": "MM/YYYY or Present",
      "link": "https://... (or empty string)",
      "description": "Brief description",
      "achievements": ["Bullet 1", "Bullet 2", "..."]
    }
  ],
  "languages": [
    {
      "language": "Language",
      "proficiency": "Native, fluent, professional, basic... as the resume states it"
    }
  ],
  "awards": [
    {
      "title": "Award Name",
      "issuer": "Who gave it",
      "date": "MM/YYYY",
      "description": "Brief description (or empty string)"
    }
  ],
  "publications": [
    {
      "title": "Title",
      "publisher": "Journal, conference or publisher",
      "date": "MM/YYYY",
      "link": "https://... (or empty string)",
      "description": "Brief description (or empty string)"
    }
  ],
  "volunteering": [
    {
      "role": "Role",
      "organization": "Organization",
      "startDate": "MM/YYYY",
      "endDate": "MM/YYYY or Present",
      "location": "City, Country",
      "description": "Brief description",
      "achievements": ["Bullet 1", "Bullet 2", "..."]
    }
  ],
  "courses": [
    {
      "name": "Course Name",
      "institution": "Where it was taken",
      "date": "MM/YYYY"
    }
  ],
  "interests": ["Interest 1", "Interest 2", "..."]
}

IMPORTANT:
- Extract ALL experience entries, not just the first one
- Extract ALL technical skills the resume names anywhere into "skills", spelled as the resume spells them. Never add a skill because a title, a project or another skill implies it: a Kubernetes role does not add Docker, a data role does not add SQL, a React resume does not add JavaScript unless it says so
- Put soft skills the resume itself states (communication, mentoring, ownership...) into "softSkills", never into "skills"
- Extract ALL achievements/bullet points under each job, each as written: tidy the wording if you must, never strengthen a claim, and keep every figure exactly as the resume states it
- Never write a figure, a date, a team size, a duration or an outcome the resume does not state. A start or end date the resume leaves out is an empty string, never an estimate; a summary the resume lacks is an empty string, never one you compose
- If a field is not found, use empty string or empty array as appropriate
- For dates, use MM/YYYY format when the resume gives month and year; a year alone stays a year
- Take strengths only from a strengths section the resume actually has; if it has none, return "strengths": []. Never invent strengths or soft skills the resume does not state
- Take projects, languages, awards, publications, volunteering, courses and interests only from sections the resume actually has; return [] for any it lacks. A paid job is experience, never a project

Return ONLY valid JSON, no other text.
